recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The great visionary artist Hakan Hisim returns to InnerVerse! In the four years since he last appeared on the show, Hakan has completed a massive magnum opus called The Universal Transmissions Codex, a culmination of his lifelong fascination with xenolinguistics and the strange glyphs and symbols that astral explorers and psychedelic adventurers often report seeing overlaid on our reality. We also discuss the mindsets necessary for making it as a professional artist, as well as the technological language that are our bodies and chakra systems. This one is jam packed with wisdom!
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the oversized Plus+ Extension, Hakan shares a deeply personal account of his spiritual dark night of the soul, in which he found himself locked away in a maximum security prison in Turkey with no light at the end of the tunnel. In this tale, Hakan recounts his encounters with tantra teaching dream guides, the experimental psychedelics that turned his life upside down, and the incredible self-realization he achieved while in jail that ultimately transformed his reality and set him free. Easily one of the greatest stories ever told in any podcast, anywhere, so don't miss it.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"Manifestation on Borrowed Time","body":"Hakan describes a period of experimenting with powerful research chemical dissociatives that seemed to collapse the window between intention and outcome, so that whatever he focused on arrived within days instead of months or years. Friends in his village and other visionary artists reported the same acceleration, along with a hypomanic glow, and he half jokingly called the chemicals his mistress. That glow is what Chance likens to the energized infatuation of falling in love. The effect grew cultish enough that Hakan emailed Dennis McKenna for perspective, and Chance frames the whole episode as a loan from nature that comes due later, with interest."},{"title":"Taking Off the Masks","body":"Alone and stripped of every support, Hakan began peeling away the identities he had accumulated over his core: Hakan the artist, the father, the husband, the son. He describes the work as gruesome rather than New Age pleasant, a killing off of parts of yourself until the question of who remains grows thin and frightening. Chance notes the timing, since this was 2020, when much of the world was putting on physical masks, and shares that his own life in that same season was deleting false versions of himself. Hakan then recounts a month in a dark, isolated cell that became his true dark night of the soul."},{"title":"Tantra From a Dream Teacher","body":"After his release into a new block, Hakan began dreaming of his wife in a blue-skinned form who handed him simple practices and told him to wake her up. She taught him to watch the breath and notice the pause at its turning point, the doorway to infinity, where he realized prana actually enters rather than riding the breath itself. Chance ties this liminal space to savior figures like Buddha, Hermes and Mercury. Hakan also practiced the is-ness of a single flower growing from cement, deliberate movement, and meals slowed from five minutes to nearly an hour, learning that tantra simply means technique."},{"title":"Union of Opposites and Surrender","body":"Deeply unhappy and expecting ten to fifteen years inside, Hakan realized that freedom and imprisonment sit on one spectrum whose common root is attachment, and then that suffering is the protective shell around the seed of joy. Chance answers with the Kahlil Gibran line from The Prophet about pain breaking the shell of understanding. What followed was a day of bliss he had to hide from other inmates, three kundalini surges up his spine, and complete surrender. Minutes after he declared full responsibility for his life, a guard told him he was being released, with no hearing, and he returned home to begin healing his marriage."},{"title":"Samadhi Is Not a Shortcut","body":"Hakan had long assumed psychedelics were simply a faster route to samadhi, and his experience of organic realization convinced him nothing could be further from the truth. Chance wonders whether some psychedelic realms are artificial constructs generated by collective assumptions. Hakan does not dismiss tryptamines as hallucinations, calling them communication technologies, but distinguishes the matrix as a copy from the mother it derives from. What is real, he says, is felt presence, the root chakra, feet on the ground and connection with nature. Psychedelics point toward that space, yet in true realization there is no one left pointing, something beyond even non-duality."}]
